title: A complex in an abelian category is exact iff the induced map to the kernel is an epimorphism
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z$ a complex of $\mathcal A$, i.e. $v\circ u=0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Let $k:K\to Y$ be a kernel of $v$ ($v\circ k=0$, and every $t:T\to Y$ with $v\circ t=0$ factors as $t=k\circ t'$ for a unique $t':T\to K$), and let $u':X\to K$ be the unique morphism with $k\circ u'=u$. Then the complex is exact at $Y$ ($\operatorname{Im}(u)=\operatorname{Ker}(v)$ as subobjects of $Y$, [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]) if and only if $u'$ is an epimorphism.

source.place: Homology, Definition 010E (label definition-exact: exact at y means Im(x->y) = Ker(y->z)) and Lemma 010C (label lemma-characterize-injective: surjective iff epimorphism, isomorphism iff injective and surjective); the statement is the combination: u factors as X ->> Im(u) >-> K, and Im(u) = Ker(v) iff the monomorphism Im(u) -> K is an isomorphism iff it is an epimorphism iff u' is one
